changes.before: "answer": "It is a funnel-shaped band of T2 and FLAIR hyperintensity tapering from thickened, blurred cortex down to the ventricular surface, and it indicates a focal cortical dysplasia, characteristically the ILAE type IIb form with balloon cells.",
changes.after: "answer": "A funnel-shaped band of T2/FLAIR hyperintensity extends from abnormal cortex towards the ventricular surface. It supports focal cortical dysplasia type II, most often IIb, but MRI does not demonstrate balloon cells or establish the histological subtype.",

changes.before: "explain": "The sign traces the path abnormal cells took during radial migration, so it runs the full thickness of the mantle from the cortical surface to the ventricular ependyma, widest at the cortex and narrowing as it descends. On isotropic 3D FLAIR it is often the only unequivocal abnormality, which is why that sequence is a protocol core. Look for its companions in the same place: cortical thickening, blurring of the grey and white matter junction, an abnormal sulcal or gyral configuration, and sometimes a deep unusually oriented sulcus at the epicentre. Its value is practical rather than descriptive. A transmantle sign identifies a discrete, resectable target with a good chance of seizure freedom, and it turns an MRI-negative patient into an MRI-positive one, which changes both the surgical decision and the odds quoted to the patient."
changes.after: "explain": "Follow the subcortical T2/FLAIR hyperintensity towards the ventricular surface and inspect the corresponding cortex on high-resolution T1. Assess cortical thickness, the grey-white junction and sulcogyral morphology in the same location. The transmantle pattern supports FCD type II, most often IIb, but does not demonstrate balloon cells or establish a histopathological subtype. Describe the lesion location and extent and relate them to the supplied electroclinical findings. Presurgical decisions require the full epilepsy evaluation."

changes.after: "detail": "Use millimetric isotropic 3D T1 for morphology, millimetric isotropic 3D FLAIR for signal, and high-resolution coronal T2 perpendicular to the hippocampal long axes for hippocampal internal architecture. Add susceptibility and other sequences for the clinical question."

clinical_fields.before: It is a funnel-shaped band of T2 and FLAIR hyperintensity tapering from thickened, blurred cortex down to the ventricular surface, and it indicates a focal cortical dysplasia, characteristically the ILAE type IIb form with balloon cells.
clinical_fields.after: A funnel-shaped band of T2/FLAIR hyperintensity extends from abnormal cortex towards the ventricular surface. It supports focal cortical dysplasia type II, most often IIb, but MRI does not demonstrate balloon cells or establish the histological subtype.

clinical_fields.before: The sign traces the path abnormal cells took during radial migration, so it runs the full thickness of the mantle from the cortical surface to the ventricular ependyma, widest at the cortex and narrowing as it descends. On isotropic 3D FLAIR it is often the only unequivocal abnormality, which is why that sequence is a protocol core. Look for its companions in the same place: cortical thickening, blurring of the grey and white matter junction, an abnormal sulcal or gyral configuration, and sometimes a deep unusually oriented sulcus at the epicentre. Its value is practical rather than descriptive. A transmantle sign identifies a discrete, resectable target with a good chance of seizure freedom, and it turns an MRI-negative patient into an MRI-positive one, which changes both the surgical decision and the odds quoted to the patient.
clinical_fields.after: Follow the subcortical T2/FLAIR hyperintensity towards the ventricular surface and inspect the corresponding cortex on high-resolution T1. Assess cortical thickness, the grey-white junction and sulcogyral morphology in the same location. The transmantle pattern supports FCD type II, most often IIb, but does not demonstrate balloon cells or establish a histopathological subtype. Describe the lesion location and extent and relate them to the supplied electroclinical findings. Presurgical decisions require the full epilepsy evaluation.
